Q1: Isopropyl ether exhibits known hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards, and organ/systemic effects. It also shows expanded hazards (Tier 2) for environmental, inhalation, and dermal/eye effects. Oral hazards are considered low to moderate (Tier 3), but data on endocrine disruption are insufficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Isopropyl ether does not appear on any official lists of concern or lists indicating low hazard.
Q3: This chemical is very well characterized, with over 9,700 scientific references and a well-defined molecular structure. While not evaluated by the EPA's most rigorous IRIS system, it does have a Provisional Peer-Reviewed Toxicity Value (PPRTV) and 77 toxicity value records, indicating significant toxicological study.
